features.name: Image opening and basic editing workflow
steps: Launch Snapseed
Select a local image
Decode and enter the editing home
Pinch to zoom, then move to view after magnifying
Long-press to compare the image before and after editing
Enter different workflows from "styles / tools / export"
The current image state is preserved when switching tools. Snapseed officially uses "choose a tool
After actually playing a previously unplayed song the play history grows and "not played recently" changes accordingly
confirm/cancel" non-destructive workflow. Google Help
features.expected: The image must be decoded and displayed correctly; zooming and panning only affect the view and do not modify the image; long-pressing must show the original image for comparison; the current edit result must not be lost when switching tools or entering export.

features.name: Looks presets
steps: Open an image
Browse several preset styles horizontally
Tap any style to preview immediately
When choosing another style the current preview is replaced
Only after ✓ does it formally enter the editing result
× restores the image from before entering the style
features.expected: Tapping a style must immediately preview the corresponding effect; choosing another must replace rather than stack; only after ✓ does the effect enter the edit stack; × must restore the state from before entering the style.

features.name: Tune Image
steps: Enter "Tune Image"
Swiping up/down selects among brightness, contrast, saturation, ambiance, highlights, shadows, and warmth
Both versions always use the same view coordinates
Multiple parameters jointly affect the current preview
After confirming, all parameters are saved as one edit step. The official classic version explicitly includes these 7 parameters. Google Help
features.expected: The 7 parameters must act on the preview independently without overriding one another; the values change continuously when swiping left/right; after confirming, all parameters are saved as one edit step and re-entering the step shows the current values.

features.name: Details
steps: Enter "Details"
Switch between "structure" and "sharpening"
Structure enhances local texture and Sharpening strengthens edge clarity
Change the value and preview in real time
The old parameter values are fixed in that edit step after confirming and will not continue to affect subsequently created Details operations. Google Help
features.expected: Structure must enhance local texture and sharpening must strengthen edges, and the two must be distinguishable; the parameters act on the preview in real time; after confirming they are fixed in the current step, and re-entering shows the saved values with new operations independent.

features.name: Curves
steps: Enter curves
Edit the overall RGB curve
Add/drag several control points
The image's brightness mapping changes in real time
Toggling the R/G/B channels can produce independent color shifts
Use presets or custom curves
After confirming the control-point state is saved with the edit step
features.expected: The curve control points must change the image's brightness mapping in real time; the RGB and per-channel curves are independent of each other; after confirming the control-point state is saved with that edit step and can be further adjusted on re-entry.

features.name: White Balance
steps: Open white balance
Adjust the temperature so the image shifts between blue/yellow
Adjust the tint so the image shifts between green/magenta
Use auto white balance or the eyedropper to select a neutral area in the image
Recompute the color from the sampled result
Confirm and save
features.expected: The temperature must change along the blue-yellow axis and the tint along the green-magenta axis; the eyedropper must recompute the white balance based on the selected pixel; the automatic and manual results act consistently on the preview and can be saved.

features.name: Crop
steps: Enter crop
Choose among free, original ratio, 1:1, DIN, 3:2, 4:3, 5:4, 7:5, 16:9, etc.
Drag an edge/corner to change the area
The constraint is maintained with a fixed ratio
After confirming, the image area seen by subsequent edits genuinely changes. The ratios listed in the official documentation match this. Google Help
features.expected: After choosing a ratio the drag must maintain that ratio constraint while free mode is unrestricted; after confirming the image area genuinely changes and affects subsequent tools; the ratio is still correct after rotating and straightening.

features.name: Rotate
steps: Open rotate
Perform a 90° rotation or straighten by a small angle with a swipe
The reference grid changes with the angle
The edges produced by rotation are handled according to the tool's rules
After confirming, subsequent text, selective, and crop operations use the new image coordinates
features.expected: Rotate and straighten must act on the preview in real time; the reference grid updates with the angle; after confirming the image coordinates genuinely change and subsequent text, selective, and crop tools use the new coordinates.

features.name: Perspective
steps: Drag to reorder or hide fields such as the start date, due date, recurrence, priority, list, tags, subtasks, reminders, description, place, file, calendar, timer, and creation date
Change the horizontal or vertical perspective by dragging/zooming
The image undergoes a geometric transformation in real time
With edge extension enabled the resulting blank area is filled automatically; when disabled the blank area remains black
After confirming, the new geometric state is passed to subsequent tools. Google Help
features.expected: The perspective transformation must act in real time and change the image geometry; with edge healing enabled the blanks are filled automatically and when disabled they remain black; after confirming the geometric state is passed to subsequent tools.

features.name: Expand Quantization
steps: Enter "expand"
Enlarge the canvas up/down/left/right respectively
Choose the padding method: smart fill, white, or black
Extend in several directions in succession
The original image stays in the correct position
After confirming the real canvas size increases and the subsequently saved new image's dimensions change in sync
features.expected: After extending, the original image must stay in the correct position; the padding method takes effect according to the selected smart fill, white, or black; after confirming the canvas size genuinely increases and the saved output image's dimensions change in sync.

features.name: Expand Advanced settings
steps: Tap the image to create a Control Point
Drag the control point to the target position
Pinch to change the affected range
The red mask shows the actually affected area
Undo the error correction
Create several more control points
Copying, moving, or deleting one point must not break the other points. The official classic Selective works exactly this way with U Point interaction. Google Help
features.expected: The control point's affected area must be visualized by the red mask and match the actual effect; each point's parameters are independent; copying, moving, or deleting one point must not break the other points' effects.

features.name: Brush
steps: Enter brush
Choose among dodge/burn, exposure, temperature, and saturation
Single-finger smearing changes only the area the strokes cover
After changing the strength new strokes use the new strength
Strength 0 erases the previous local effect
Opening the mask preview shows the painted area in orange. Google Help
features.expected: Only the stroke-covered area is affected and untouched areas stay as they are; after changing the strength new strokes use the new strength; with strength 0 the existing local effect must be erased; the mask preview accurately reflects the painted area.

features.name: Healing
steps: Zoom in on the image
Tap or paint over stains, clutter, or small-object areas
Generate replacement content from the surrounding pixels
Heal several positions in succession
Import an image
After the zoom ratio changes the screen touch still maps to the correct original-image area
After confirming the healing result enters the final image
features.expected: Healing must generate replacement content based on surrounding pixels without obvious seams; continuous healing and Undo are supported; after zooming or panning the touch still maps to the correct original-image area; after confirming, the result is kept in the final image.

features.name: HDR landscape HDR Scape
steps: Choose the HDR style
Perform "play next" on another song D
Adjust parameters such as filter strength, brightness, saturation, and smoothing respectively
The shadow and highlight detail change at the same time
After switching to another HDR style, that style's parameters are used for the preview
Saved after confirming. Google Help
features.expected: Different HDR styles must produce discernible tone-mapping differences; the parameters affect the preview in real time; after switching the style that style's parameters are used and are saved as a complete filter step after confirming.

features.name: Glamour Glow
steps: Enter glamour glow
Choose different soft-glow presets
Adjust glow, saturation, and warmth
The highlights spread softly and the overall tone changes with the parameters
Multiple parameter combinations stay within the same filter step. Google Help
features.expected: Glow must produce a soft highlight-spread effect; saturation and warmth act independently; switching presets replaces the current parameters; after confirming all parameters are saved in the same filter step.

features.name: Tonal Contrast
steps: Enter tonal contrast
Adjust the local contrast of highlights, midtones, and shadows independently
Use "protect shadows / protect highlights" to reduce detail loss in dark or bright areas
Other parameters are preserved when any one is adjusted
Confirming forms the complete effect. Google Help
features.expected: The highlight, midtone, and shadow adjustments must each affect the corresponding brightness range; protect-shadows and protect-highlights must reduce detail loss in the corresponding areas; other parameters are preserved when any one changes; all are saved together after confirming.

features.name: Drama
steps: Choose different Drama styles
Each style uses a different local-contrast look
Adjust Strength to change the dramatic degree
Adjust Saturation to control the color
Switching presets replaces the current Drama preview in real time rather than stacking a new Drama. Google Help
features.expected: Different styles must use different local-contrast looks; Strength changes the dramatic degree and Saturation controls the color; switching presets must replace the current preview rather than stacking a new effect.

features.name: Vintage
steps: Choose different vintage-film styles
Adjust brightness, saturation, style/texture, and vignette
Move/change the vignette's affected area
Randomizing the texture produces another texture position

After confirming, that randomization result should be kept rather than re-randomized on reopening. The official Vintage also includes controls such as Style, Brightness, Saturation, Texture, and Vignette. Google Help
features.expected: Different styles produce different film looks; the vignette area can be moved and acts on the corresponding position; randomization produces another texture position and is fixed after confirming, and reopening must not re-randomize.

features.name: Grainy Film
steps: Browse several film presets
Choose a film color style
Adjust the grain intensity and style strength independently
The grain change should not be simply equivalent to an overall noise brightness change
After confirming, the preset and parameters together form the filter state
features.expected: The grain intensity must only add a grain effect and must not be equivalent to an overall brightening or noise change; the style strength independently controls the film tone; after confirming, the preset and parameters together form the filter state.

features.name: Retrolux
steps: Choose the retro style
Adjust effects such as brightness, saturation, contrast, Style, scratches, and light leaks
Randomization can change the light-leak/scratch positions
The random parameters are fixed after the same confirmation
Only re-generating produces another result
features.expected: The scratch and light-leak positions change with randomization and are fixed after confirming; reopening must not re-randomize; each parameter acts on the preview independently; switching styles replaces the current effect rather than stacking.

features.name: Grunge
steps: Enter Grunge
Adjust Style to change the overall color distribution
Adjust brightness, contrast, saturation, and Texture Strength
Randomly change the texture position and angle
The current random texture is saved as part of that edit step. The official documentation states that Grunge can randomize the texture angle/position and provides these parameters. Google Help
features.expected: Style must change the overall color distribution; Texture Strength controls the texture intensity; randomization changes the texture position and angle and is fixed after confirming; the parameter combination is saved with that edit step.

features.name: Black & White
steps: Convert to black and white
Choose several black-and-white presets
Adjust brightness, contrast, and grain
When choosing red/yellow/green/blue color filters, different original colors map to different gray levels
Switch presets to recompute without deleting the original color information. Google Help
features.expected: Different color filters must map different original colors to different gray levels; brightness, contrast, and grain act independently; the tool is non-destructive and the original color information must be preserved for undo.

features.name: Noir
steps: Choose the Noir style
Produce a heavier darkroom/cinematic look than ordinary black-and-white
Adjust related effects such as brightness, Wash/print feel, and grain
When switching from Noir back to ordinary black-and-white the two tools keep independent parameters and edit steps
features.expected: Noir must produce a heavier darkroom/cinematic look than ordinary black-and-white; its brightness, wash, and grain parameters are saved independently; it exists as a separate edit step from ordinary black-and-white and switching does not override one with the other.

features.name: Face retouching / Face
steps: Start face retouching on an image containing a face
Automatically detect the face
Choose a preset lighting or skin-tone effect
Adjust face brightening, skin smoothing, and eye clarity respectively
The change occurs only around the detected face
An image without a face should not fake a fixed face region. The official classic Face provides these three core control parameters. Google Help
features.expected: The face-detection result must determine the affected area and the effect must appear only in the detected face region; an image with no face must not produce a fixed-area effect or crash; the brighten, smooth, and eye-clarity parameters are independent and saved.

features.name: If elevation data exists show the elevation profile with cumulative ascent/descent
steps: Enter head pose on a photo with a recognizable face
Drag to change the character's left/right/up/down head direction
Adjust the available portrait parameters such as smile and pupils
The deformation should be centered on the actual facial features
After confirming the portrait geometry result is kept and Undo can restore the original pose
features.expected: The deformation must be performed around the detected facial features, with the drag direction corresponding to the head turn; after confirming the geometric result is kept and can be restored with Undo; reasonable feedback is required when there is no valid face.

features.name: Lens Blur
steps: Enter lens blur
Switch between linear and elliptical focus
Drag the focus
Pinch to change the focus area's size, shape, and rotation
Adjust the blur strength, transition range, and vignette
Only the area outside the focus gradually blurs. Google Help
features.expected: Only the area outside the focus becomes blurred while the focus stays sharp; the focus area's size, shape, and rotation change with the pinch gesture; the strength, transition range, and vignette act independently and can be saved.

features.name: Vignette
steps: Open vignette
Drag the blue center point to decide the theme position
Pinch to change the center area's size
Adjust the outer brightness and inner brightness respectively
The center and edges form independent brightness effects
The center position and parameters are preserved when re-entering after editing. Google Help
features.expected: The center point's position determines the vignette center, and pinching changes the center area's size; the outer and inner brightness act independently; after confirming, the center position and parameters are preserved when re-entering.

features.name: Double Exposure
steps: Select a second image over the current image
The second image is added as an independent compositing layer
Move, scale, and reposition
Switch between different blend modes
Adjust the opacity
After confirming a composite result is formed
The first original image remains intact after Undo
features.expected: The second image must be overlaid as an independent layer and can be moved and scaled into position; the blend mode and opacity act on the composite in real time; after Undo the first original image must be fully restored.

features.name: Text, frames, and the final editing lifecycle
steps: Use "text" to enter content
Choose different layout templates
Change the color and move/scale/rotate the text; then use "frame" to choose a border style and adjust the width
The two effects are stacked in the order they were applied

Afterwards Undo/Redo, viewing previous modifications, and saving/exporting genuinely produce a final image with all visual effects. The official documentation explicitly states that the tool order affects the final result, e.g. a frame before or after lens blur gives different results, and that editing uses a non-destructive workflow. Google Help
features.expected: Text and frames must be stacked in the order applied, and a different order should give a different final effect; Undo and Redo correctly step back and restore; the export must genuinely produce a final image containing all visual effects.
